Reasoning: Regard the child and the sled as a whole; the forces include: gravity mg downward, the support force N of the ground on the sled upward, the pulling force F along the rope obliquely upward to the right, and the kinetic friction force f of the ground on the sled horizontally to the left. Since the sled moves at a constant speed along the horizontal ground, the acceleration is 0, so the forces are balanced in both the horizontal direction and the vertical direction. Horizontal direction: f = F cosθ = 100 × 0.8 = 80 N. Vertical direction: N + F sinθ = mg, so N = mg - F sinθ = 38 × 10 - 100 × 0.6 = 380 - 60 = 320 N. From the kinetic friction formula f = μN, obtain μ = f / N = 80 / 320 = 0.25.

As shown in the figure, a child is sitting on a sled, and an adult is pulling the sled with a force of magnitude $F=100\mathrm{N}$ at an angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ to the horizontal, causing the sled to move at a constant speed along the horizontal ground. The mass of the child together with the sled is $m=38\mathrm{kg}$, and $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ is taken. $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

3. The coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu$ between the sled and the ground

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: the image shows the child and sled on level horizontal ground, with the adult pulling by a rope directed upward and to the right; the dashed horizontal line and marked angle θ show that the applied force F makes angle θ above the horizontal. Read from the text F=100 N, θ=37°, m=38 kg, g=10 m/s², sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, and that the sled moves at constant speed. Draw a free-body diagram for the sled-child system: weight mg downward, normal N upward, pulling force F at angle θ forward/upward, and kinetic friction f backward. Since constant speed means zero acceleration, impose equilibrium in x and y: horizontally, f=F cosθ=100×0.8=80 N; vertically, N+F sinθ=mg, so N=38×10−100×0.6=320 N. Then use the kinetic-friction relation f=μN to get μ=80/320=0.25.

claims.claim: The child and sled as a whole are subjected to a pulling force F along the rope, obliquely upward to the right.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The pulling force F is along the rope, obliquely upward to the right

claims.claim: The child and sled as a whole are subjected to a kinetic friction force f horizontally to the left.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The kinetic friction force f exerted by the ground on the sled is horizontally to the left

claims.claim: When the sled moves at a uniform speed along the horizontal ground, the acceleration is 0.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Since the sled moves at a uniform speed along the horizontal ground, the acceleration is 0

claims.claim: The forces on the sled are balanced in the horizontal direction.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the forces are balanced in both the horizontal direction and the vertical direction

claims.claim: The forces on the sled are balanced in the vertical direction.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Therefore the forces are balanced in both the horizontal direction and the vertical direction

claims.claim: Force balance in the horizontal direction gives f = F cosθ = 100 × 0.8 = 80 N.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Horizontal direction: f = F cosθ = 100 × 0.8 = 80 N

claims.claim: Force balance in the vertical direction gives N = mg - F sinθ = 38 × 10 - 100 × 0.6 = 320 N.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: Vertical direction: N + F sinθ = mg, so N = mg - F sinθ = 38 × 10 - 100 × 0.6 = 380 - 60 = 320 N

claims.claim: The formula for kinetic friction is f = μN.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: From the formula for kinetic friction f = μN
